chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashm narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Ziyad, who said: The Imam (peace be upon him) said:
He who claims to know us while holding fast to a rope other than ours is lying.

key_terms.أَنَّهُ يَعْرِفُنَا: That he knows us (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: The Truthful (title of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, the 6th Imam)
key_terms.عُرْوَةٍ: A rope/handle, metaphorically referring to a source of authority or means of connection

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'holding fast to a rope other than us' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the claimants of knowledge who rely on external authorities rather than the Ahl al-Bayt, establishing the Imams as the exclusive 'Urwah al-Wuthqa' (firm handhold). This underscores the Shia epistemological principle that true understanding of the divine message and the Imams' station is derived solely through their guidance, rejecting independent or rival sources of authority. The hadith thus serves as a foundational criterion for distinguishing authentic Shia scholarship from those who claim proximity to the Imams while following other paths.
